title: Choose the visual world for Dr Aloka's Eye Care
question: The roll assigned the Sankranti Kite Sky. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Sankranti Kite Sky
options.lineage: Makar Sankranti kite-flying over Hyderabad rooftops
options.thesis: Flying a kite needs two aligned eyes and depth judgement: the page is a child learning to follow one kite across a clearing sky.
options.viewport: Dusk over Kukatpally rooftops; a single kite seen doubled and blurred until scroll pulls the two images into one. Headline and Book key sit on the rooftop line.
options.risk: Festival imagery can read as seasonal decoration if the clinical proof below is set timidly.

raised.raise: Colour obeys a law: marigold appears only after the child meets the doctor, and it is reserved for hope and the Book action.
One unbroken manja thread runs the whole page as the journey rail, always marking where 'now' is: fear, hope, treatment, joy.
Total environmental commitment: the sky itself carries the emotion, from dusk to clear noon, with no card shells over it.
One pull transforms: the scroll is the thread, and tugging it re-aligns the doubled kite into a single sharp one.
Exactly one committing control per viewport, the Book key; everything else stays quiet.

options.label: The Stereo Fly
options.lineage: Titmus fly stereo test used in the clinic's binocularity work-up
options.thesis: Depth appears only when both eyes work together: the page is flat and grey until it resolves into true 3D.
options.viewport: A flat, doubled plate that snaps into stereo depth on pointer or scroll, with the fly's wings lifting off the page.
options.risk: The closest to what clinical eye-care sites already gesture at; the anaglyph can tire the eyes of low-vision visitors.

options.label: Printing-House Calendar
options.thesis: A painted plate of doctor and child above; a tear-off date pad below that books the visit.
options.viewport: The painted plate fills the top; the pad shows this month, with Sundays greyed as closed.
options.case: Every Indian home knows the form; it holds on audience identification, but the fear-to-joy story fits it less clearly.
options.risk: Needs commissioned painting; with photos alone it reads as a nostalgia costume.

options.label: Arcade Pixel Glow
options.viewport: A pixel stage with a score bar.
options.case: Loses both axes: parents do not identify with it and it obscures the clinic.
options.kept: Palette as law: one colour reserved for the moment that matters.

options.label: Drum-Machine Step Row
options.thesis: The journey as a sixteen-step pattern.
options.viewport: A step row under a chase light.
options.risk: Reads as a toy instrument, not a clinic.
options.kept: One unbroken timeline row that always shows where 'now' is.

options.label: Bioluminescent Wake
options.viewport: A black field with glowing trails.
options.risk: Dark, low-contrast and hard for low-vision visitors.
options.kept: Total environmental commitment: the ground itself carries the emotion.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.thesis: One pull turns flat into volume.
options.viewport: A black semicircle and a gold cord.
options.kept: One pull transforms the whole composition.

options.label: Creator Hardware Bench
options.viewport: A keycap grid with one orange key.
options.risk: Cold and gadget-like for a children's clinic.
options.kept: Exactly one committing key per view.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A trusted-clinic homepage: doctor portrait hero, service grid, stats, testimonials, map, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Doctor portrait beside headline and Book button, with credentials beneath.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other eye hospital in Hyderabad by design.
